title: Control plane: add ShadowTrafficPolicy schema + validation + migration scaffolding
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Adds control-plane schema and validation for ShadowTrafficPolicy (disabled by default) to support upcoming shadow-traffic quality evals; includes migration scaffolding for attaching shadow policies to routes/rollouts.
description: Summary: This PR introduces the control-plane schema for ShadowTrafficPolicy and wiring needed to store/validate it in route/rollout configs. This is the first building block for shadow traffic (mirroring sampled requests to one or more shadow targets) and is intentionally scoped to schema/validation + migration scaffolding only (no data-plane mirroring, no telemetry). Motivation: We need a stable, versioned policy object that can be attached to routes and rollout variants, validated at write time, and safely no-oped until the data plane and telemetry paths are enabled. This keeps the upcoming work (ENG-5402/5403/5404) unblocked while making sure we don’t paint ourselves into a corner on defaults, RBAC, and security-sensitive fields. What’s included: (1) New schema objects: ShadowTrafficPolicy v1 and ShadowTargetRef. (2) Validation: sampling is bounded; max shadow targets enforced; timeouts bounded; mutually exclusive fields validated; required metadata controls validated. (3) Migration scaffolding: adds optional shadow_traffic_policy field to RoutePolicy and RolloutVariantPolicy (behind a feature flag gate) and includes a config migration stub to allow future move/rename without breaking existing configs. (4) Example configs and golden tests for JSON serialization. Non-goals: data plane mirroring behavior (ENG-5402), deterministic fingerprinting/bucketing (ENG-5403), telemetry schema + ingestion (ENG-5404), and retention/redaction implementation (ENG-5411). Design notes / defaults: Default is disabled unless explicitly enabled; fail_open defaults true (shadow path must never impact user response); sampling_mode is “deterministic” but bucketing implementation is not in this PR; shadow request headers default to allowlist-only and we explicitly disallow copying Authorization/Cookie by default; shadow targets are references (model_id / deployment_id / routing_policy_id) to avoid embedding large objects and to keep cardinality sane. Key fields (v1): enabled (bool), sampling_rate (0.0–1.0), sampling_mode (deterministic|bernoulli), max_shadow_targets (enforced globally), shadow_targets[] (target_ref + weight + per-target timeout_ms), request_copy (allowlist headers + metadata keys), fail_open (bool), shadow_deadline_ms (overall), tags (limited set; validated against allowlisted keys), created_by/updated_by (populated by control-plane). Tests: adds schema validation unit tests (happy path + boundary/invalid cases), JSON round-trip tests, and a migration test that ensures older configs without shadow_traffic_policy still parse with identical semantics. Rollout plan: This lands gated; no runtime behavior change until the routing layer consumes the policy (ENG-5402). After merge, we’ll start dogfooding in internal tenants with feature flag enabled in the control plane only.
commits: control-plane/schema: add ShadowTrafficPolicy v1 + ShadowTargetRef types
control-plane/config: attach optional shadow_traffic_policy to route + rollout variant policies (flag-gated)
control-plane/migrations: add v1 migration scaffolding + golden tests
docs(internal): add example configs + field-level comments
review_conversation: Ethan Park: Can we make sure defaults are safe and do not accidentally enable shadowing when configs are partially specified? Specifically: if enabled is omitted, do we treat it as false? Also, please clamp/validate sampling_rate and enforce max targets at validation time, not in the consumer. Benji Okafor (author): Yup—enabled defaults false. Added explicit validation requiring enabled=true to allow any shadow_targets, otherwise we reject configs that try to specify targets while disabled (prevents accidental partial enable). sampling_rate is validated [0,1]. max_shadow_targets enforced at write time. Jordan Lee: Request copy semantics: we should not allow arbitrary header copy at first; please implement an allowlist and add validation to block known sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie, X-Api-Key). Also, tags need a bounded set so we don’t blow up cardinality downstream. Benji Okafor: Implemented header allowlist + explicit denylist for sensitive headers; validation errors include which header violated policy. Tags validated against allowlisted keys and max length; also limit to 10 tags. Paula Mendes: For Rollouts integration, do we attach this to the RoutePolicy or per-variant? We’ll need per-variant for comparing candidate variants vs control. Benji Okafor: Added optional shadow_traffic_policy field to both RoutePolicy (base) and RolloutVariantPolicy (override). RoutePolicy is the baseline; variant policy can override (e.g., add a new shadow target). Consumers can resolve effective policy via existing merge semantics. Marcus Lin: Please add audit fields placeholders (created_by, updated_by) but do not accept them from user configs; server should set. Also confirm that we’re not persisting raw prompts here. Benji Okafor: Added created_by/updated_by as server-populated fields (ignored on input); confirmed policy schema contains only routing/config knobs—no payload. Marcus Lin: LGTM once the input-ignore behavior is covered by a test. Benji Okafor: Added test for server-side fields not being accepted on input + updated docs comment. Ethan Park: One more: set fail_open default true and ensure we have an upper bound on shadow_deadline_ms (to avoid accidental huge timeouts). Benji Okafor: Done—fail_open default true; shadow_deadline_ms must be <= 2000ms and per-target timeout_ms <= 1500ms, both configurable later but bounded for beta safety. Ethan Park: Approved. Jordan Lee: Approved. Marcus Lin: Approved.
